llmSchema.title: What the model sees
llmSchema.intro: The tool schema sent to the model when it calls this tool. Everything else is resolved by the engine before the model is involved.
llmSchema.visibleHeading: The parameters below are filled by the model
llmSchema.visibleEmpty: Nothing. The engine resolves every field.
llmSchema.noInstruction: No instruction written; the model only sees 'Template variable: {name}'
llmSchema.tableWins: (saved variable: if the table has a value at call time it replaces the model’s answer, unless Overridable is on; if the table is empty, the model’s answer is sent as the fallback)
llmSchema.hiddenHeading: The parameters below are filled by the system; the model never sees them
llmSchema.reasonDropped: not sent (empty, a sibling field has a value)

fieldFate.explainAiFills: The agent decides this value at call time and sends it. It has no fixed value here.
fieldFate.explainFromVariable: This value comes from a saved workflow variable. The engine fills it before the call, so the agent never sees or changes it. To let the agent override it, turn on Overridable under "Description & allowed values".
fieldFate.explainFromVariableOverridable: Normally filled from the saved variable, but Overridable is on: if the agent supplies a value, the agent's value wins for this call.
fieldFate.explainFromVariableLifted: This value comes from a variable produced during the call, so the model still sees the parameter in its schema. At call time the saved value replaces the model's answer; if extraction produced nothing, the model's answer is sent as the fallback.
fieldFate.explainFromVariableNoModel: This action runs automatically when the node is entered, without the model. The engine fills this field from the saved variable; the model is not involved and cannot override it.
fieldFate.explainFromVariableOverridableLifted: The model sees this parameter in its schema. If it supplies a value, that value wins for this call; otherwise the saved variable fills it.
fieldFate.explainFixed: A fixed literal value. It is sent as-is on every call and the agent cannot change it.
fieldFate.explainPerCall: A dynamic system value (like a fresh id or the current date). The engine generates it new on each call.
fieldFate.explainRaw: This is code. Its placeholders are not substituted here; the code reads variables at runtime via vars[...].
fieldFate.explainDropped: This field has no value while a sibling field does, so the engine sends the body without it: it is neither baked nor asked of the AI. Give it a value or a {{variable}} to include it.
fieldFate.explainDroppedNoModel: This action runs automatically when the node is entered, without the model, so there is nobody to fill an empty value: the field is simply not sent. Give it a value or a {{variable}}.
fieldFate.explainUnknown: You wrote {{...}} referencing a variable, but no saved variable with that name exists in this workflow ({names}). At call time the engine cannot fill it, so the agent fills the value instead. If that is intended, fine; if not, use an existing variable.
fieldFate.explainUnknownNoModel: You wrote {{...}} referencing a variable, but no saved variable with that name exists in this workflow ({names}). This action runs automatically without the model, so nothing fills it and the field is not sent. Use an existing variable or a fixed value.
fieldFate.explainUnknownNoModelMixed: No saved variable named {names} exists, and this action runs without the model, so nothing can fill it. Because the value mixes other text, the field IS still sent, with the literal {{...}} text left in, a broken payload. Fix the name or remove the placeholder.

nodeForm.agentTooltip: Select an agent whose voice and LLM config will be used for this node.
nodeForm.entryBehaviorTooltip: Controls what happens when the conversation enters this node. LLM generates a contextual entry message, TTS speaks a fixed message.
nodeForm.entryTtsDescription: Plays a fixed message on entry
nodeForm.entryAudioCaptionHelp: Committed to the conversation so the model sees what the user heard. Defaults to a generic placeholder when blank.
nodeForm.audioAssetEmpty: No audio assets yet. Click Upload to add one.
nodeForm.audioAssetNotFound: Selected asset not found. Pick another.
nodeForm.entryTextPlaceholder: Text to speak on entry, e.g. Hi, is this {{customer_name}}?

nodeForm.rolePromptTooltip: System prompt that defines the agent's persona and tone for this node.
nodeForm.postHistoryPromptTooltip: Injected after the chat history on every turn of this node. Supports {{variables}}, put values that change during the call here to keep them out of the cached prompt prefix.
nodeForm.dialoguePromptTooltip: Instructions for what this node should accomplish.
nodeForm.loopConditionTooltip: Describes when the agent should keep looping in this node. When matched, the agent stays and skips transition evaluation.
nodeForm.loopConditionPlaceholder: e.g. The caller has not yet provided all required information...
nodeForm.maxTurnsTooltip: Limit back-and-forth exchanges in this node. When the limit is reached, auto-transitions to the selected target.
nodeForm.truncationStrategyTooltip: Controls how conversation history is managed. "Keep All" retains the full history. "Keep Recent" drops older turns beyond the window size. "Summarize" compacts older turns into a summary, keeping only the most recent turns in full.
nodeForm.truncationWindowSizeTooltip: Number of recent conversation turns to keep in full. With "Keep Recent", older turns are dropped. With "Summarize", older turns are compacted into a summary.
nodeForm.skipUserTurnTooltip: When enabled, the node speaks its entry message but does not wait for user input. It immediately evaluates its transition conditions and routes to the matching target.
nodeForm.passthroughTooltip: When enabled, the node does not interact with the user. It immediately evaluates its transition conditions and routes to the matching target.
nodeForm.interruptionsTooltip: Controls when the user can barge in while the agent is speaking in this node. Allowed: barge-in anywhere. Protect first message: the entry message cannot be interrupted. Protect entire node: no agent message in this node can be interrupted; the user can still reply once the agent finishes speaking.
nodeForm.returnToPreviousOnInterrupt: Return to Previous Node on Interrupt
nodeForm.returnToPreviousOnInterruptHint: When the user interrupts the farewell/transfer message, return to the previous node instead of ending the conversation.
nodeForm.onEnterFirstEntryOnly: Run entry only on first visit
nodeForm.onEnterFirstEntryOnlyTooltip: When on, this node plays its entry message only the first time the call reaches it. If the conversation returns to this node later, the entry is skipped and the node uses its regular prompt.
nodeForm.disableInactivityMonitorTooltip: When enabled, the silence timeout is paused while in this node. The agent will not prompt the user for inactivity.
nodeForm.confidenceReaskOverrideTooltip: Override the agent-level low-confidence re-ask gate for this node. Auto follows the agent setting (and skips the re-ask on digit nodes); Always forces it on; Never forces it off.
nodeForm.smartTurnOverrideTooltip: Override the agent-level Smart Turn (turn-taking) model for this node. Auto follows the agent setting (and falls back to VAD on digit nodes); Always forces Smart Turn on; Never uses VAD-only turn detection. Only applies when Smart Turn is enabled for the agent.
nodeForm.reasoningOverrideTooltip: Let the model think before answering while this node is active. Improves accuracy on hard steps but adds latency. Works only with vLLM-family LLM endpoints whose chat template supports thinking (e.g. gemma-4); other providers ignore it. Auto leaves thinking off, which is how the agent runs by default.
nodeForm.digitNodeOverrideTooltip: Force this node to be handled as a digit-collection node, regardless of its variable types. Useful when an ID/phone/date field is typed as text. Affects Smart Turn auto-disable and the STT re-ask gate. Auto uses variable-type detection. (Holding number bursts into one turn is the separate “Hold turn for digit entry” toggle below.)
nodeForm.digitContinuationTooltip: Don’t end the turn the moment the caller pauses, keep it open so they can finish a multi-part answer (a long number read in bursts, or any answer with pauses). Turns on the controls below.
nodeForm.expectedDigitsTooltip: End the turn the instant this many digits are recognized on a digit node (e.g. 11 for a TC kimlik), instead of waiting out the pause window, the agent replies the moment the number is complete. Leave empty to wait for the normal end of turn. Streaming STT only.
nodeForm.digitHoldSecsTooltip: How long to keep the turn open after the caller pauses, before ending it. Overrides the agent default. If an expected count or field type is set and reached, the turn still ends right away.
nodeForm.digitHoldRulesTooltip: When the caller's words so far match a pattern, keep the turn open at least this many seconds (e.g. a trailing "ve…", "şey…", or "bir saniye"). Matches any words, not just numbers. Only extends the wait; it never cuts a turn short.
nodeForm.digitHoldRuleInvalid: Won't be saved until valid (needs a pattern and 0.1–5 seconds).
nodeForm.expectedFieldKindsTooltip: For a node collecting several different-length numbers (e.g. TC kimlik = 11, phone = 10, date of birth = 8) in one place, pick the types here instead of a single expected digit count. The turn ends the instant the digits form a complete, valid value of one of these types, each fires at its own length without cutting off a longer one. Using the type’s checksum/prefix to tell them apart. Supersedes the expected digit count above. Streaming STT only.
nodeForm.idleConfigTooltip: Override the global silence timeout behaviour for this node. When not configured, the agent-level call settings apply.
nodeForm.idleConfigEnable: Override global silence timeout for this node
nodeForm.idleConfigSilenceTimeoutTooltip: How long (in seconds) to wait for user input before triggering a check-in. Overrides the global setting for this node. Leave at 0 to use the global default.
nodeForm.idleConfigMaxRetriesTooltip: How many times to check in with the user before taking the exhaust action. Default is 2.
nodeForm.idleConfigCheckInMessageTooltip: Message to say when the user is silent. Leave blank to let the assistant generate it.
nodeForm.idleConfigClosureMessageTooltip: Message to say before taking the exhaust action. Leave blank to let the assistant generate it.
nodeForm.idleConfigClosureMessagePlaceholder: e.g. I'll let you go for now, feel free to call back.
nodeForm.idleConfigOnExhaustTooltip: What the agent should do after all check-in attempts fail.
nodeForm.idleConfigRouteTargetTooltip: The node to route to when retries are exhausted.
nodeForm.blockConversationDuringApiCallTooltip: When enabled, the agent stops speaking and waits for the API call to complete before continuing. When disabled, the API call runs in the background and the agent continues immediately.
nodeForm.suppressToolResults: Compact tool results in LLM context
nodeForm.suppressToolResultsTooltip: When enabled, tool call and result messages are replaced with compact system messages before sending context to the LLM, saving tokens. Extraction variables are still captured from raw results.
nodeForm.extractionVariablesTooltip: Variables to extract from the conversation. Extracted values can be used in transition conditions, API calls, and other nodes.
nodeForm.variableDescriptionPlaceholder: AI instruction: Guides the agent on what to extract from the conversation
nodeForm.apiStatusCodeDescription: HTTP status code from API call

beforeCall.label: Before the call
beforeCall.body: Supplied from outside the agent before the first word, a campaign column, a SIP header, a start-of-call tool, or your test value. If nobody sends it, the placeholder is read out loud exactly as you typed it.

conversation.label: From the conversation
conversation.body: An extraction model listens for this while its node is the current node. It has no value before that node runs, and it is rewritten on every turn that node is active, so a later node can overwrite it silently.

tool.label: From a tool
tool.body: A tool writes this when it runs. Nothing here has a value until that call actually completes, and one API call can create names you never declared.

platform.label: Platform value
platform.body: The platform computes this. You can use it but not change it, and some of these are frozen at the moment the call started.

afterCall.label: After the call
afterCall.body: This only exists once the conversation is over. An end-of-call tool can read it; nothing during the call can.

template.label: Prompt section
template.body: This is a block of prompt text the engine generates, not a value. It only means anything inside the specific prompt override you are editing.

finding.noProducerPrompt: Nothing sets {name}. The agent will read the braces out loud.
finding.noProducerToolOnly: Nothing sets {name}, and this field is nothing but that placeholder, so the field is removed from the request entirely.
finding.noProducerToolMixed: Nothing sets {name}. The literal braces are sent to your API inside this field.
finding.noProducerCondition: Nothing sets {name}. The comparison comes out false every time, with no error.
finding.noProducerCode: Code is never substituted. {name} is passed to Python as-is and will raise a SyntaxError.
finding.rawField: Code is never substituted. {name} reaches Python as literal text and will raise a SyntaxError, read the value with vars[…] instead.
finding.spacedName: Remove the spaces inside the braces. The engine matches the text exactly.
finding.twoWriters: Written by more than one node, the last one to run wins.
finding.setLater: {name} is written by {node}, which only runs after this point. Here it is still empty.
finding.notEveryPath: {name} is only written on some routes into this node. A call arriving via {path} finds it empty.
finding.notEveryPathNoRoute: {name} is only written on some routes through the workflow, so it can be empty here.
finding.globalOnly: {name} is only written by the global node {node}, which may never trigger. Treat it as optional.
finding.stopsAtSubAgent: {node} hands the call to another agent, which can add or change any variable. Availability cannot be checked past this point.
finding.wrongSurface: {name} only works in {allowed}. Here it stays as raw text.
